## Counselling Process Guide

**Round 1:** First allotment based on NEET AIR and choices. You can Accept (freeze), Float (upgrade attempt), or Slide (upgrade within same institute).

**Round 2:** Vacant seats from Round 1 + newly added seats. Can change preferences. Important for upgrades.

**Mop-up Round:** For seats remaining after Round 2. Open to fresh candidates too (who didn't participate earlier). Usually the last regular round.

**Stray Round:** Final round. Colleges may directly admit from a list. Usually walk-in basis.

**Options after allotment:**
- **Freeze:** Accept the allotted seat. No further upgradation.
- **Float:** Accept but allow upgradation to higher preference in next round.
- **Slide:** Accept but allow upgradation within the same institute only.

**Pro tip:** Always choose "Float" in Round 1 unless you got your top choice. This keeps upgrade possibilities open.

## Required Documents for NEET Counselling

Here's your complete checklist:

### Document Checklist

**Domicile / Residence Certificate** [Online Registration] — Conditional
Format: PDF
Required for state quota. Proves 10-15 years continuous residence. Not needed for AIQ.

**Income Certificate** [Online Registration] — Conditional
Format: PDF
Required for EWS (below 8 LPA). Also needed for some fee concessions.

**PwD Certificate** [Online Registration] — Conditional
Format: PDF
Required for PwD quota seats. Must be from designated government authority with 40%+ disability.

**Migration Certificate** [Physical Reporting] — Conditional
Format: Original
Required for AIQ/Deemed if studied in different state from allotted college.

**Anti-Ragging Affidavit** [Physical Reporting] — MANDATORY
Format: Stamp Paper
Both student and parent sign. Generate at antiragging.in. Two copies required.

**Class 10th Marksheet & Certificate** [Online Registration] — MANDATORY
Format: PDF/JPEG
For DOB verification. Name must match NEET application.

**Class 12th Marksheet & Certificate** [Online Registration] — MANDATORY
Format: PDF/JPEG
Must show PCB + English aggregate. Min 50% (40% for reserved).

**Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC/EWS)** [Online Registration] — Conditional
Format: PDF
OBC must have non-creamy layer clause, issued within last year. EWS certificate valid for one financial year.

**Gap Year Affidavit** [Physical Reporting] — Conditional
Format: Stamp Paper
Required if there is a gap year between Class 12 and admission. Notarized on stamp paper.

- Exam conducted by NTA (National Testing Agency)
- Single exam for all medical/dental colleges in India (except AIIMS & JIPMER which now merged)
- Pen-and-paper based exam (OMR sheet)
- Duration: 3 hours 20 minutes
- Total marks: 720 (180 questions × 4 marks each, -1 for wrong answer)

**Government vs Private Medical Colleges — Key Differences:**

| Factor | Government | Private/Deemed |
|--------|-----------|----------------|

| **Total MBBS cost** | Rs 1-8 Lakh | Rs 30-1.5 Crore |
| **Patient load** | Very high (great exposure) | Moderate |
| **Infrastructure** | Varies (some old) | Usually modern |
| **Faculty** | Experienced, may be overburdened | Good ratio, more accessible |
| **Clinical exposure** | Excellent (high OPD/IPD) | Good but less volume |
| **Bond** | Some states have bond (2-5 yrs) | Usually no bond |
| **Hostel** | Basic but cheap | Better amenities, costlier |

**Bottom line:** If you can get a government seat, it's almost always the better choice financially. A government college MBBS degree is valued equally (sometimes more) by employers and PG exam committees.

**Exception:** Top deemed universities like KMC Manipal, CMC Vellore offer excellent education but at premium fees.

**MBBS vs BDS — Should You Choose BDS?**

**MBBS:**
- 5.5 years (4.5 + 1 year internship)
- Better long-term career prospects
- Higher earning potential
- More PG specialization options
- More competitive (lower closing rank needed)

**BDS:**
- 5 years (4 + 1 year internship)
- Easier to get admission (higher closing rank)
- Good career in private practice
- Fewer PG seats available
- Lower initial investment in private practice setup

**Our recommendation:** If your rank allows MBBS in a government college, always prefer it. Consider BDS only if:
- Your rank doesn't qualify for MBBS anywhere
- You have genuine interest in dentistry
- Private college MBBS is unaffordable

**Never drop a year just for MBBS** if you have a government BDS seat — unless you're very confident about improving your rank significantly.
